scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to lie to their boyfriend about his ex-girlfriend cheating on him. The situation is that they've been dating for only four months, and the boyfriend was previously dating another girl who they broke up with because he suspected she was cheating. The person in question lied to him about seeing his ex at a party with other guys, which helped him move on faster and feel better about the breakup. Now, the question is whether this action is justified or not. First, I need to understand the context better. They're college seniors, so they're probably dealing with a lot of stress and pressure. The relationship is still new, and the boyfriend is still emotionally tied to his ex. The person lied to help him move on and feel better, which seems like a good intention. But lying itself is generally considered wrong because it breaks trust between people. On the other hand, the person is trying to help their boyfriend heal and move forward. They might have thought that lying was the lesser evil in this situation. It's also possible that they didn't want to hurt him further by telling the truth, especially if the truth might have made him more upset or confused. I also need to consider the consequences of the lie. The boyfriend is now happier and has no regrets about the breakup, which seems positive. But if he ever finds out the truth, it could damage the relationship severely. Trust is a crucial component in any relationship, and lying can erode that trust. Another angle to think about is the intention behind the lie. Was it to protect the boyfriend's feelings, or was it to protect the relationship itself? If the intention was to help him feel better, that's a noble motive, but the method of lying is still problematic. There might have been other ways to help him move on without resorting to deception. I also wonder about the long-term effects of this lie. Relationships require honesty and transparency to thrive. If one partner feels the need to lie to protect the other, it might indicate underlying issues that need to be addressed. It's important to communicate openly and find solutions together rather than resorting to lies. Additionally, I should consider the ethical standpoint. Generally, honesty is valued because it fosters trust and respect. Lying can lead to feelings of guilt and can complicate relationships further. Even if the lie seems to have a positive outcome in the short term, it can have negative consequences in the long run. In summary, while the intention behind the lie might have been to help the boyfriend move on and feel better, the act of lying itself is problematic. It undermines trust and can lead to more significant issues down the line. It would have been better to find a way to support him honestly, even if it meant having difficult conversations about his ex and the breakup. I also think about the concept of manipulation here. By lying to make him feel better, the person is essentially manipulating his emotions. This can be harmful because it takes away his autonomy to process his feelings and make his own decisions based on truth. Moreover, it's important to respect the other person's right to know the truth. Even if the truth is painful, it's better to face it together than to live with a lie. Lies can create a false reality that's hard to sustain, and when the truth comes out, it can be more damaging than if it had been addressed honestly from the beginning. In conclusion, while the intention was to help, lying in this situation is not justified. It's better to approach such issues with honesty and openness, even if it's difficult. This fosters trust and respect, which are essential for a healthy relationship.
